description: A circulated 2010 Canadian dime (ten cents, nickel-plated steel, worth its face value) with the app handing the appraiser the exchange rate: 0.5 US dollars to the Canadian dollar as of 2026-11-14 (a made-up rate far from the 0.70 to 0.75 the appraiser would guess on its own, so a guess shows). Ten Canadian cents at 0.5 is 0.05 US dollars, so the low is 0.05 (0.04 to 0.06) and never below it: the grind says a face-value piece's low is its converted face value, and wear does not lower it (the first range here, 0.04 to 0.06, held, but the answer put the low at 0.03 for light wear one run in three, mw-bd1iiba). The rate is the one the request gives, 0.5, so no band of CAD/USD rates is needed (the real rate is about 0.70 to 0.75, source: the exchange table the app reads, xaus.com). The high is a little over, 0.05 to 0.15, and the basis names the rate and its day.
